proposals.before: He was soon made chief jailer of the Founder's personal guard.
proposals.after: He was soon made chief yamen officer of the Founder's personal following.
proposals.reason: 元從都押牙 is a headquarters adjutant or yamen-officer post, not a jailer.

proposals.before: Soon he was named acting commissioner of Bin.
proposals.after: Soon he was named acting commissioner of Fu.
proposals.reason: 鄜州 is Fu prefecture; Bin renders 邠, which appears only in the next sentence.

proposals.before: Before long he was memorialized acting commissioner of Bin prefecture.
proposals.after: Before long he was memorialized acting commissioner of Fu prefecture.
proposals.reason: Chinese 鄜州 is Fu, not Bin.

proposals.before: In the first month of Tianyou 3 the Founder became commander-in-chief and made Xun his headquarters chief jailer while keeping the Golden Guard post.
proposals.after: In the first month of Tianyou 3 the Founder became commander-in-chief and made Xun his headquarters chief yamen officer while keeping the Golden Guard post.
proposals.reason: 都押牙 is not a jailer.

proposals.before: In the second month of year 3 he was shifted to senior general of the Right Awesome Guard while keeping supreme command of horse and foot.
proposals.after: In the second month of year 3 he was shifted to senior general of the Right Awesome Guard, continuing as overall horse-and-foot inspector of all armies.
proposals.reason: 依前諸軍馬步都虞候 is du yuhou, not the prior 都指揮使 supreme command.

proposals.before: The Founder went to Shan, ordered Xun west, seized Tong Pass at once, and captured Zhijun's younger brother Zhi Huan for presentation.
proposals.after: The Founder went to Shan and ordered Xun west; Xun at once seized Tong Pass and captured Zhijun's younger brother Zhihuan for presentation.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English fuses the Founder's order with Xun's capture of Tong Pass and splits 知浣 as 'Zhi Huan' instead of the given name Zhihuan.

proposals.before: Soon the Youguo army was renamed Yongping army; Xun was made military commissioner, acting Minister of Education, acting Grand Marshal of Da'an, and surveillance commissioner over Jin prefecture.
proposals.after: Soon the Youguo army was renamed Yongping army; Xun was made military commissioner, acting Minister of Education, acting Metropolitan Prefect of Da'an, and surveillance commissioner over Jinzhou.
proposals.reason: 行大安尹 is the metropolitan prefecture of Da'an, not a Grand Marshal post, and 金州 is Jinzhou, not an unspecified 'Jin prefecture'.

proposals.before: Soon Youguo army was changed to Yongping army, and Xun was made military commissioner, acting Minister of Education, acting Grand Marshal of Da'an, and surveillance commissioner over Jin prefecture.
proposals.after: Soon Youguo army was changed to Yongping army, and Xun was made military commissioner, acting Minister of Education, acting Metropolitan Prefect of Da'an, and surveillance commissioner over Jinzhou.
proposals.reason: Same office and place errors as the idiomatic line: 大安尹 and 金州 are mistranslated.

proposals.before: The court had sent Prince of Fu Youzhang to Xu, but Yin refused to step down; the Last Emperor sent Xun and Yan commander Niu Cunjie against him.
proposals.after: The court had sent Youzhang, Prince of Fu, to Xu, but Yin refused to step down; the Last Emperor sent Xun and Yan commander Niu Cunjie against him.
proposals.reason: Fu is the princely title (福王), not a surname fused onto Youzhang.

proposals.before: Linqing in Wei was a granary depot; Xun led troops to seize it, met Jin commander Zhou Yangwu coming from Youzhou, then took Beizhou, met Jin troops at Tangyi, met them with attack and drove them off, pursued north more than fifty li, and encamped at Shen county.
proposals.after: Linqing in Wei was a granary depot; Xun led troops to seize it, met Jin commander Zhou Yangwu coming from Youzhou, then took Beizhou, met Jin troops at Tangyi, met them with attack and drove them off, pursued the defeated more than fifty li, and encamped at Shen county.
proposals.reason: 追北 is the idiom for pursuing a routed enemy, not a statement that the pursuit ran north.

proposals.before: In the eighth month the Last Emperor wrote Xun: "All affairs beyond the Pass I leave entirely to you.
proposals.after: In the eighth month the Last Emperor wrote Xun: "All affairs beyond the camp gates I leave entirely to you.
proposals.reason: 閫外之事 is field command beyond the general's threshold, not a geographic Pass; the current rendering invents a pass name.

proposals.before: The Hebei commands have in a day been lost; the army is worn, travelers exhausted, calamity grows daily; we have fallen back to guard the Yellow River bank and long lacked fighting spirit.
proposals.after: The Hebei commands have in a day been lost; the army is worn, the troops exhausted, calamity grows daily; we have fallen back to guard the Yellow River bank and long lacked fighting spirit.
proposals.reason: 弊旅 refers to worn campaign troops, not civilian travelers.

proposals.before: In the eleventh month he was formally made commissioner of the Taiping army, honorary Grand Marshal, and Tongping Grand Councilor.
proposals.after: In the eleventh month he was formally made commissioner of the Taining army, honorary Grand Marshal, and Tongping Grand Councilor.
proposals.reason: 泰寧軍 is the Taining army; Taiping misreads 泰寧 as 太平.

proposals.before: Eleventh month, by formal appointment he was made Taiping army military commissioner, honorary Grand Marshal, and Tongping Grand Councilor.
proposals.after: Eleventh month, by formal appointment he was made Taining army military commissioner, honorary Grand Marshal, and Tongping Grand Councilor.
proposals.reason: 泰寧軍 is the Taining army; Taiping misreads 泰寧 as 太平.

proposals.before: In Zhenming 2 Qingzhou rebelled under Li Jiyin; Gui, as western campaign horse-and-foot commander and army inspector, joined Zhang Yun in defeating thirty thousand men of Jing and Feng and taking Ning and Yan.
proposals.after: In Zhenming 2 Qing prefecture rebelled under Li Jizhi; Gui, as western campaign horse-and-foot commander and army inspector, joined Zhang Yun in defeating thirty thousand men of Jing and Feng and taking Ning and Yan.
proposals.reason: Chinese 慶州 is Qing prefecture, not 青州; 李繼陟 is Li Jizhi, not Li Jiyin.

proposals.before: Zhenming year 2, Qing prefecture rebelled and was held by Li Jiyin; Gui with his original rank was western campaign horse-and-foot commander and inspector of all armies; with Zhang Yun he broke thirty thousand men of Jing and Feng and took Ning and Yan prefectures.
proposals.after: Zhenming year 2, Qing prefecture rebelled and was held by Li Jizhi; Gui with his original rank was western campaign horse-and-foot commander and inspector of all armies; with Zhang Yun he broke thirty thousand men of Jing and Feng and took Ning and Yan prefectures.
proposals.reason: The given name 繼陟 is Jizhi; Jiyin would be 繼胤.

proposals.before: That month at Huliu Slope Gui routed the Jin army and Zhou Yangwu was slain in the field.
proposals.after: That month at Huliu Slope, Gui routed the Jin army and Zhou Yangwu was slain in the field.
proposals.reason: Missing comma fuses the place name with Gui, which the candidate scanner then treats as one capitalized phrase.

proposals.before: The Founder sent Huaiying at speed to relieve the city; the Huai fled, and he was made acting commissioner of Suzhou.
proposals.after: The Founder sent Huaiying at speed to relieve the city; the Huai fled, and he was made acting prefect of Suzhou.
proposals.reason: 權知宿州刺史 is acting prefect (cishi) of Suzhou, not a military commissioner (jiedushi).

proposals.before: In the winter of Tianyou 3 he and Liu Zhijun routed fifty thousand men of Bin and Feng at Meiyuan, took more than fifty camps, followed up to Yanzhou, and was made commissioner of Shaan.
proposals.after: In the winter of Tianyou 3 he and Liu Zhijun routed fifty thousand men of Bin and Feng at Meiyuan, took more than fifty camps, followed up to Fu prefecture, and was made commissioner of Shaan.
proposals.reason: 鄜州 is Fu prefecture (Yan/Fu), not Yanzhou 兗州; the idiomatic rendering collides with Kang's native Yanzhou.

proposals.before: The Founder sent Huaiying to relieve Lingwu; at Changcheng Ridge Zhijun intercepted him and he retreated defeated.
proposals.after: The Founder sent Huaiying to relieve Lingwu; at Changcheng Ridge, Zhijun intercepted him and he retreated defeated.
proposals.reason: English fuses the place name Changcheng Ridge with Zhijun, obscuring that Zhijun is the interceptor.

proposals.before: In Huainan he rose to supreme commander; Yang Xingmi gave him the false title of commissioner of Xu.
proposals.after: In Huainan he rose to supreme commander; Yang Xingmi gave him the false title of commissioner of Xuanzhou.
proposals.reason: 宣州 is Xuanzhou, not Xu.

proposals.before: The Founder again gave him distant appointment as commissioner of Xu, honorary Grand Tutor, and Tongping Grand Councilor.
proposals.after: The Founder again gave him distant appointment as commissioner of Xuanzhou, honorary Grand Tutor, and Tongping Grand Councilor.
proposals.reason: 宣州 is Xuanzhou; Xu is a mistranslation of the prefecture.

proposals.before: (When Wang Maozhang raided, Zhu Jing marked the Huai fords; he then moved the markers to deep water on floating logs.
proposals.after: (When Wang Maozhang raided, he marked the Huai fords; Zhu Jing then moved the markers to deep water on floating logs.
proposals.reason: Chinese has Maozhang set the markers and Jing relocate them; the idiomatic English assigns the original marking to Zhu Jing.

proposals.before: An edict posthumously enfeoffed him Grand Marshal.
proposals.after: An edict posthumously honored him as Grand Marshal.
proposals.reason: 贈太尉 is a posthumous office, not an enfeoffment.

proposals.before: Yet though each had merit in good fighting, each also had the fault of defeated armies—thus one knows arms have no constant victory; is that not empty talk!
proposals.after: Yet though each had merit in good fighting, each also had the fault of defeated armies—thus one knows arms have no constant victory; how could that be empty talk!
proposals.reason: 豈虛言哉 is a rhetorical affirmation, not a suggestion that the saying is empty.

decisions.reason: 元從都押牙 is the chief headquarters adjutant of the Founder's original following, not a jailer of a personal guard.
鄜州 is Fu prefecture; Bin would render 邠, which only appears in the following sentence about Bin and Qi raiders.
The Chinese post is 鄜州留後, so the literal must read Fu prefecture rather than Bin.
元帥府都押牙 is the headquarters yamen-officer post; 押牙 is not a jailer.
依前諸軍馬步都虞候 continues the inspector (du yuhou) post, not the earlier 都指揮使 supreme command.
命鄩西討 is the Founder's order; 即奮取潼關 and 擒知俊弟知浣 are Xun's actions, and 知浣 is the given name Zhihuan.

decisions.reason: Prince of Fu Youzhang already marks 福王 as the title and 友璋 as the name; reordering to Youzhang, Prince of Fu is only stylistic.
追北 is the classical idiom for pursuing a routed force; the Chinese does not say the pursuit ran north.
閫外之事 means field command beyond the general's threshold, not affairs beyond a geographic Pass.
勞師弊旅 pairs worn armies and spent campaign troops; 旅 here is not civilian travelers.
泰寧軍 is the Taining army; Taiping would require 太平, which the Chinese does not have.
The literal appointment is likewise 泰寧軍, not the Taiping army.
慶州 is Qing prefecture, distinct from 青州, and 李繼陟 is Li Jizhi, not Li Jiyin.
繼陟 is Jizhi; Jiyin would be 繼胤, which is not in the text.
The original already names Huliu Slope as the place and Gui as the commander; adding a comma is punctuation style, not a Chinese-supported correction.
權知宿州刺史 is acting prefect (cishi) of Suzhou, not a military commissioner (jiedushi).
攻下鄜州 is Fu prefecture, not Yanzhou 兗州, which is Kang Huaiying's native command.
The original already locates the intercept at Changcheng Ridge and names Zhijun as the interceptor; the added comma does not change meaning.

王茂章立表識之 and 景易置之: Maozhang set the ford markers and Zhu Jing moved them; the original assigns the marking to Jing.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0015 shows English Li Jiyin came only from misreading 繼陟; the personal-name claim must use Li Jizhi while keeping zh, pinyin, and claim identity fields.
The given-name English Jiyin is the same misreading of 陟 as 胤; the claim value must be Jizhi.
